title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Tree
statement_short: Given a binary tree, find the lowest common ancestor of two given nodes p and q. The lowest common ancestor is defined as the lowest node in the tree that has both p and q as descendants.
constraints: 2 <= number of nodes in tree <= 10^5, -10^9 <= Node.val <= 10^9, p != q, p and q exist in the tree
hint: Node count up to 10^5 requires an O(n) post-order recursion, returning the current node when p or q is found.
keywords: has both p and q as descendants
why_not: Right: Tree DFS recursively checks left and right subtrees post-order, returning the root when p and q match opposite subtrees in O(n) time and O(h) space. Not Tree BFS: Level-order traversal using queue tracking requires storing parent pointers for all nodes using extra O(n) memory. Not Union-Find: Disjoint-set forest algorithms solve offline query batches, but post-order DFS directly finds LCA for single queries. Not Binary Search: The input is a general binary tree rather than a sorted binary search tree.
